name: UNHCR-Mandate Refugee/Asylum-Seeker Registration (No Domestic Legal Status)

requirements.blocker_text: Libya is NOT a party to the 1951 Refugee Convention or its 1967 Protocol. It has ratified the 1969 OAU Convention Governing the Specific Aspects of Refugee Problems in Africa, but 'has yet to implement [it] through the adoption of asylum-related legislation or procedures' (source's own wording) -- Libya has NO domestic asylum law at all, joining the pattern found for Haiti, Cuba, and Afghanistan earlier in this dataset. This dataset's build found a materially more severe version of that pattern here: all non-Libyans, including refugees and asylum-seekers, are legally classified as 'illegal immigrants' under national immigration law, illegal entry/exit is criminalized, and this results in documented arbitrary, indefinite detention without due process or access to alternatives. UNHCR registers asylum-seekers and refugees at the Serraj Registration Centre in Tripoli and issues its OWN certificates entirely under its international mandate -- these certificates do not themselves confer legal residence status under Libyan domestic law and do not prevent the detention risk described above.
requirements.fix_path: Register with UNHCR Libya (appointment required at the Serraj Registration Centre, Tripoli, or via phone/WhatsApp); this dataset could not confirm that registration itself provides protection from arrest or detention under Libyan domestic law.

outcome.duration_length: UNHCR mandate certificate; no fixed domestic legal validity period exists

sources.title: UNHCR Rights Mapping and Analysis Platform -- Libya's non-accession to the 1951 Convention/1967 Protocol, ratification but non-implementation of the 1969 OAU Convention, classification of non-Libyans as illegal immigrants, criminalization and detention
UNHCR Help Libya -- operational registration process at the Serraj Registration Centre, Tripoli
